analysis: Only scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py changed (offline CI scoping test). The head test file (lines 89-220) now pins a thin dev caller workflow: push-to-dev only, with paths matching release-swift.yml, no dispatch/inputs/ref, one job guarded by refs/heads/dev that calls ./.github/workflows/release-provider.yml with environment dev and `secrets: inherit`. It also pins the reusable workflow's dev path (lines 172-220): unguarded secrets must be the Apple signing set (only in build-and-release) or DEV_*; Developer ID signing, notarization and stapling; fan helper verified against the Apple-team requirement; per-environment publication concurrency. The change is a test file with no runtime, provider, coordinator or key-handling code, so it does not touch the provider threat-model assets or boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/011/012, T-041 and others), and nothing is invalidated. The lane itself changes materially: from ad-hoc self-signed branch builds to Developer ID signing on dev pushes. That change lives in the workflow files, which are not supplied here. Residual questions for integration, not findings: (1) The test checks the workflow files the PR also modifies, and the test's own CI wiring is not shown. (2) `secrets: inherit` hands all repo secrets, including prod ones, to the reusable workflow. The test relies on regex guards (GUARDED_SECRET) in release-provider.yml to keep prod secrets from reaching the dev path. Those regexes are heuristic: a prod secret read under some other expression form would hit the assertIsNotNone check and fail, which is fail-closed. (3) Whether the dev lane can reach Apple signing and notarization secrets from a dev branch push, and whether branch protection on `dev` is adequate, cannot be judged from this unit. A reviewer of the workflow files should verify both. No concrete regression is visible in the supplied lines.
